sentences.cn_text: 在2006年的电影《穿普拉达的女王》中，梅丽尔·斯特里普饰演的米兰达·普里斯特利斥责她那位毫不起眼的助手，因其以为高级时尚与自己无关。
sentences.en_text: In the 2006 film version of The Devil Wears Prada, Miranda Priestly, played by Meryl Streep, scolds her unattractive assistant for imagining that high fashion doesn’t affect her.

sentences.cn_text: 普里斯特利解释了助手毛衣上的深蓝色是如何在多年间从时装秀流向百货商店，最后到达这个可怜女孩无疑淘得这件衣服的打折货架。
sentences.en_text: Priestly explains how the deep blue color of the assistant’s sweater descended over the years from fashion shows to department stores and to the bargain bin in which the poor girl doubtless found her garment.

sentences.cn_text: 这种自上而下的时尚商业观念已完全过时,与伊丽莎白·克莱恩在《过度着装》中描绘的狂热世界格格不入,该书是她对「快时尚」长达三年的控诉。
sentences.en_text: This top-down conception of the fashion business couldn’t be more out of date or at odds with the feverish world described in Overdressed, Elizabeth Cline’s three-year indictment of “fast fashion.”

sentences.cn_text: 在过去十年左右的时间里,技术进步使得Zara、H&M和优衣库等大众市场品牌能够更快速地应对潮流趋势,更精准地预测需求。
sentences.en_text: In the last decade or so, advances in technology have allowed mass-market labels such as Zara, H&M, and Uniqlo to react to trends more quickly and anticipate demand more precisely.

sentences.cn_text: 更快的周转意味着更少的库存积压、更频繁的产品发布和更高的利润。
sentences.en_text: Quicker turnarounds mean less wasted inventory, more frequent releases, and more profit.

sentences.cn_text: 这些品牌鼓励注重风格的消费者将服装视为一次性物品——虽然它们不会明说,但这些衣服只能洗一两次——并每隔几周就更新衣橱。
sentences.en_text: These labels encourage styleconscious consumers to see clothes as disposable — meant to last only a wash or two, although they don’t advertise that — and to renew their wardrobe every few weeks.

sentences.cn_text: 克莱恩认为,通过以极低价格提供流行单品,这些品牌劫持了时尚周期,撼动了长期习惯于季节性节奏的产业。
sentences.en_text: By offering on-trend items at dirt-cheap prices, Cline argues, these brands have hijacked fashion cycles, shaking an industry long accustomed to a seasonal pace.

sentences.cn_text: 当然,这场变革的受害者不仅限于设计师。
sentences.en_text: The victims of this revolution, of course, are not limited to designers.

sentences.cn_text: 为了让H&M能够在其全球2300多家门店中销售售价5.95美元的针织迷你裙,它必须依赖低工资的海外劳工,下达消耗自然资源的大额订单,并使用大量有害化学品。
sentences.en_text: For H&M to offer a $5.95 knit miniskirt in all its 2,300-plus stores around the world, it must rely on low-wage overseas labor, order in volumes that strain natural resources, and use massive amounts of harmful chemicals.

sentences.cn_text: 《过度着装》是时尚界对迈克尔·波伦的《杂食者的困境》等消费维权畅销书的回应。克莱恩认为:「大规模生产的服装与快餐一样,满足了饥饿和需求,但却不耐久且造成浪费。」
sentences.en_text: Overdressed is the fashion world’s answer to consumer-activist bestsellers like Michael Pollan’s The Omnivore’s Dilemma. “Mass-produced clothing, like fast food, fills a hunger and need, yet is non-durable and wasteful,” Cline argues.

sentences.cn_text: 她发现,美国人每年购买约200亿件服装——人均约64件——无论他们捐出多少,这种过量最终都导致浪费。
sentences.en_text: Americans, she finds, buy roughly 20 billion garments a year — about 64 items per person — and no matter how much they give away, this excess leads to waste.

sentences.cn_text: 在《过度着装》接近尾声时,克莱恩介绍了她的理想典范,一位名叫萨拉·凯特·博蒙特的布鲁克林女性,自2008年以来她自己制作所有衣服——而且做得非常漂亮。
sentences.en_text: Towards the end of Overdressed, Cline introduced her ideal, a Brooklyn woman named Sarah Kate Beaumont, who since 2008 has made all of her own clothes — and beautifully.

sentences.cn_text: 但正如克莱恩首先指出的,博蒙特花了数十年才完善自己的手艺;她的榜样无法被轻易复制。
sentences.en_text: But as Cline is the first to note, it took Beaumont decades to perfect her craft; her example can’t be knocked off.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管包括H&M在内的几家快时尚公司已采取措施遏制其对劳工和环境的影响——如推出绿色环保系列——克莱恩相信持久改变只能由消费者促成。
sentences.en_text: Though several fast-fashion companies have made efforts to curb their impact on labor and the environment — including H&M, with its green Conscious Collection line — Cline believes lasting change can only be effected by the customer.

sentences.cn_text: 她展现出许多可持续发展倡导者共有的理想主义,无论是在食品还是能源领域。
sentences.en_text: She exhibits the idealism common to many advocates of sustainability, be it in food or in energy.

sentences.cn_text: 虚荣心是恒定的;只有当人们无力承担不可持续消费的代价时,才会开始更可持续地购物。
sentences.en_text: Vanity is a constant; people will only start shopping more sustainably when they can’t afford not to.
